# Klartex

> PDF generation via LaTeX — structured data in, professional documents out.

Klartex is an open-source CLI tool and Python library that generates professional PDF documents from JSON data. It uses XeLaTeX under the hood.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install klartex
```

Requires XeLaTeX: `brew install --cask mactex` on macOS, or on Debian/Ubuntu `apt install texlive-xetex texlive-fonts-recommended texlive-latex-extra texlive-latex-recommended texlive-science texlive-plain-generic`.

## Generate a PDF

```bash
# Write JSON data to a file, then render
klartex -t faktura -d invoice.json

# Or pipe JSON via stdin
echo '{"invoice_number": "2026-001", ...}' | klartex -t faktura
```

## Available templates

- `_block` — Universal block engine. The agent composes the document freely from typed blocks.
- `balansrakning` — Balance sheet with assets and liabilities+equity sections.
- `budgetrapport` — Budget report with account codes, budgeted amounts, and actuals.
- `faktura` — Invoice with line items, VAT, and payment info.
- `kvitto` — Receipt with line items, total, and payment method.
- `protokoll` — Meeting minutes with agenda, decisions, and adjusters.
- `resultatrakning` — Income statement with comparison years and optional notes.
- `sie-exportrapport` — Human-readable PDF of SIE4 accounting data.

## Get the JSON Schema for a template

```bash
klartex schema faktura
```

## Invoice example (template: faktura)

```json
{
  "invoice_number": "2026-001",
  "date": "2026-02-15",
  "due_date": "2026-03-17",
  "sender": {
    "name": "Mitt Företag AB",
    "org_number": "556999-8888",
    "address_line1": "Storgatan 1",
    "address_line2": "123 45 Stockholm"
  },
  "recipient": {
    "name": "Kundföretaget AB",
    "org_number": "556123-4567",
    "address_line1": "Storgatan 1",
    "address_line2": "123 45 Stockholm"
  },
  "lines": [
    {
      "description": "Consulting services",
      "quantity": 40,
      "unit": "hrs",
      "unit_price": 1200.00,
      "vat_percent": 25
    }
  ],
  "bankgiro": "1234-5678",
  "note": "Thank you!"
}
```

Save as `invoice.json`, then run: `klartex -t faktura -d invoice.json`

## Block engine example (template: _block)

```json
{
  "lang": "en",
  "body": [
    { "type": "heading", "text": "My Document" },
    { "type": "text", "text": "Hello world." },
    {
      "type": "signatures",
      "parties": [
        { "name": "Company AB", "signatory": "Anna Andersson" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Save as `doc.json`, then run: `klartex -d doc.json`

## Block types (for _block template)

agenda, budgettabell, callout, clause, columns, description_list, form, heading, latex, list, name_roster, notapparat, page_break, parties, quote, resultatrakning, signatures, table, text, title_page

Use `klartex schema _block` to get the full JSON Schema, or query individual block schemas via the HTTP API at https://app.klartex.se (`GET /api/blocks`, `GET /api/blocks/{name}/schema`).

## Page setup and branding in recipes

Every recipe template accepts `page_template` in object form, the same shape the block engine uses: two independent slots, `header` and `footer`, alongside the document-level settings `font` and `header_font` (fontspec family names; `header_font` falls back to `font`), `page_numbers`, `first_page_header` and `diff_style`. Each slot is `null` for empty, a variant name, or an object with `variant` and that variant's settings. Header variants are `letterhead` (organisation details on the left, logo on the right; `fields.org_name` is required in the object form) and `logo` (logo only). Footer variants are `pagenumber` (page number, preceded by the document title when `title` is set) and `columns` (three aligned columns of company, contact and payment details in `fields`). A slot left out takes the surface's default: an empty header and the page-number footer on the block engine, the letterhead header and the page-number footer with the document title in recipes.

`faktura` and `kvitto` require `sender` with `name` (the issuer, shown in a block beside the recipient; without `logo`, `sender.name` is also set as a wordmark in the logo slot), and take `logo` / `logo_height` / `logo_offset` in the header. Their default footer is the `columns` variant, derived from `sender` (name, address, org number) and the payment fields `bankgiro` / `plusgiro` / `iban` / `bic`; a column whose data is missing is rendered with a grey label (*Betalningsuppgifter saknas*, *Org.nr saknas*, *Adress saknas*) rather than dropped. Company, contact and payment details belong in `page_template.footer.fields` — a `page_template.footer` sent by the producer is merged key by key over the derived one, and there is no top-level `footer` on these recipes (the schema rejects it and points at the slot).

## Page templates: per-call or registered

`POST /api/render` takes a body of `{"template": "<template name>", "data": { ... }, "page_template": "<registered bundle name>"}`. Template data goes inside `data` — including `page_template` in object form, which is part of the template schema. The top-level `page_template` field is either a string naming a bundle registered on the server, or a page-template object, which is passed through as `data.page_template`. A bundle name inside `data` fails schema validation with `400`.

A bundle carries one `.tex.jinja` describing the whole page. It reaches the renderer as the header slot's source with the footer set to `null`, so the bundle owns both slots: a `header` or a `footer` sent in `data.page_template` gives way. The document-level settings there — `font`, `header_font`, `diff_style`, `page_numbers` and `first_page_header` — still apply.

`page_template` in object form travels with the request — font, header font and footer are part of the data, so a call is self-contained and needs no account.

A named page template — a reusable bundle with a logo and its own LaTeX fragment, referenced as `page_template: "<name>"` — is registered once at `POST /api/page-templates` and lives on the server. Writing to that registry requires a bearer token, so it answers `401` without one. Access is granted on request until self-serve accounts launch — email kontakt@klartex.se. `GET /api/page-templates` returning an empty list is the expected state, not a fault; use the object form until you have a bundle.

`GET /api/blocks`, `GET /api/templates`, their `/schema` variants and `POST /api/render` need no token — with one exception. The `latex` block passes raw LaTeX to the compiler, so an anonymous render containing one answers `403` with a `detail` that names the block (`"type": "token_required"`, `"block_type": "latex"`) and points `path` at it. A token unlocks the full block surface; it does not raise the rate limit, which applies per IP either way.

## Change marking

For documents that show what changed between two versions — the canonical case is amending statutes — mark edits inline using git word-diff notation. `{+added text+}` renders green, `[-removed text-]` red and struck through. The markers work in every field that passes through inline formatting, including table cells.

Whole paragraphs take `revision` on the `text` block instead: `"revision": "added"` or `"revision": "removed"`.

`page_template` accepts `diff_style`: `"color"` (default) marks additions in green text, `"underline"` marks them with a green underline. Removals are struck through either way. Underline-against-strikethrough is the convention in amendment documents and, unlike colour, survives black-and-white printing.

## Number formatting

Amounts and quantities render in Swedish style by default (`32 400,00` — thin-space grouping, decimal comma). The document language picks the style; `number_format` (`sv` or `en`) in `faktura` / `kvitto` data overrides it.
